## Which file do I need?

| You want to… | Download |
|---|---|
| Play straight away on any computer | **cognitive-terrain-0.16.html**, then double-click it to open in your browser |
| Read the rules | **Cognitive-Terrain-Field-Manual-0.16.pdf** |
| Run it for a group, build campaigns, see why it works | **Cognitive-Terrain-Practitioners-Manual-0.16.pdf** |
| Hear each week read aloud (optional) | the **Immersive Briefings** voice pack, on its own release: **voice-emma-1** |
| Install it like a normal program | **…-Setup.exe** (Windows), **…-macOS-AppleSilicon.zip** or **…-macOS-Intel.zip** (Mac), **…-Linux.tar.gz** |
| Host it on itch.io | **…-web.zip** |

The installers are not code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS warn on first
launch. **PLAYTEST-README.txt** explains how to get past the warning.

Two-player games work between any of these files, as long as both players
use version 0.16.

## What's new

- **Immersive Briefings: optional narration.** A new setting that uses a
  free voice pack, downloaded separately. The game does not change without
  it, and the setting stays off until you load the pack.
  - With the voice pack loaded, the week in review opens with a short
    broadcast, read aloud. The broadcaster is whichever side is ahead on
    Decision Health: Blue Public Broadcast, Olvana Central Television or
    Donovia First.
  - Each broadcast is built from that week's real moves: the leader's best
    story, the other side's failures, areas won or lost, and the crisis ahead.
  - The text is shown as captions while it plays.
  - The voice ("Emma, UK") is synthetic speech, generated on your computer by
    an open-source model. It works offline and nothing is sent anywhere.
  - Load it once from Settings › Immersive Briefings, or put it beside a
    downloaded game before you start it. You can remove it from the same
    place.
  - The game checks every file in the pack against fingerprints built into
    the game before using it.
- **Narration plays on.** If you continue before the broadcast ends, it
  carries on into the next week, with a small ON AIR tab to stop it.
- **Designer's note.** Cognitive warfare is a contest of narratives, and every
  week in this game happens twice: once on the board, and once in how each
  side tells it. Immersive Briefings let you hear that second version. When
  you are winning, you hear your own side's calm account. When you are losing,
  you hear the other side's broadcaster telling your public that its leaders
  cannot decide, built from the moves you just watched. I made it optional on
  purpose. The base game has to stay small, quiet and offline for the
  classrooms, exercise rooms and locked-down networks where it is played.
  The voice is for players who want the war of narratives in their ears as
  well as on the map. *Kevin Williamson*
- Narration is single-player only (two-player games skip the week in review).
- **Two manuals.** The Field Manual is now only what a player needs. A new
  **Practitioner's Manual** is for facilitators and instructors:
  - running a session, from a lunch break to an exercise across several
    organisations;
  - choosing campaigns and difficulty for a learning goal, and leading the
    debrief;
  - the campaign and technology editors;
  - setting up the room;
  - design notes on each mechanic: what it models, how it was arrived at, and
    its sources.
  The campaign editor page moved there.
- **Field Manual:** a new page on Immersive Briefings, Kokoro, ONNX Runtime
  and eSpeak NG on the credits page, and the two-player page now says Red.
- No rule changes. Two-player codes work between 0.16 builds.
